questions.prompt: What is the key difference between String and &str in Rust?

options.a: They are identical types, differing only in mutability keywords
options.b: String owns heap memory and can grow; &str is a borrowed fixed view
options.c: &str lives on the heap, String lives on the stack

questions.prompt: Why do idiomatic Rust APIs prefer taking &str parameters instead of &String?

options.a: It is purely a performance optimization for small strings
options.b: &str accepts strictly more callers (String borrows via deref coercion, string literals, and slices) at zero cost
